standardSilverside.source: r/southafrica thread, Jul 2026 — "Retail bulk silverside is currently R130-150/kg". Midpoint taken. The same thread also notes "at R599/kg that is based on a raw beef price of around R200/kg", which is a useful independent sanity check.

wagyuTrimmed.source: ASSUMPTION — SA A-grade wagyu strip at wholesale, trimmed for biltong. NOT sourced. This is the number most likely to be wrong, which is exactly why the break-even table is printed.

finishedYield.label: kg finished biltong per kg raw beef
finishedYield.source: ASSUMPTION — wet-to-dry weight loss in curing. 1 kg raw -> 0.35 kg finished. Sensitive: every 0.05 of yield moves finished cost by roughly R130/kg.

spicesMarinadeRarPerKg.source: ASSUMPTION — salt, coriander, chilli and cure packaging, per kg finished.

coldChainDispatchRarPerKg.source: ASSUMPTION — vacuum sealing, cold store, courier dispatch, per kg finished.

qaOverheadRarPerKg.source: ASSUMPTION — hygiene, QA and labour overhead allocated per kg finished.

packagingRarPerKg.label: Packaging per kg finished, by line and pack
packagingRarPerKg.source: ASSUMPTION — Luxury 500g pouch + label R9.50; Luxury 1kg valve bag R14; Gold 1kg = 14 x 70g resealable pouches at R4.20 each (R58.80/kg, so R59); Gold 7kg case = 100 x 70g bulk liners (R420 per 7kg, so R60/kg). The two lines genuinely cost different to pack, which is part of why Gold can carry a premium.

goldLineRatio.label: Gold 1kg price as a multiple of Luxury 1kg
goldLineRatio.source: DERIVED from the live Shopify ladder: Gold 1kg R1,450 / Luxury 1kg R650 = 2.2308. This is a MARKET/BRAND relationship, not a cost one — the R45/kg packaging gap explains only 5% of it, so the rest is positioning. The proposal preserves the ratio rather than inventing a new architecture, then checks whether the result still clears the floor.

marginFloorPct.source: POLICY — 25%, matching the wholesale coffee sheet and the caviar desk floor. A ladder below this is not a ladder.

smallPackPremiumCap.source: POLICY — the per-kg premium a smaller pack may carry over the 1kg, capped at 15%. Market check: Woolworths charges R157.99 for 150g against R279.99 for 400g — a 50% per-kg premium at the snack end, roughly 25% at the 400g end. 15% is the disciplined number for a fresh-protein brand, not a confection.

caseSavingPct.source: POLICY — the 7kg case must be at least 8% cheaper per kg than 7 x 1kg. The buyer has to be able to count the saving, or the case is a decoration.

roundingZar.source: POLICY — published prices round to the nearest R5.

fx.source: frankfurter.dev (ECB reference) 2026-10-29; cross-check exchangerate-api 16.6339 — agree within 0.04%. Higher of the two used.
